[size=5][b]English[/b][/size]

Press [b]G[/b] to open your warehouse anywhere and [b]V[/b] to deposit backpack items into their categories. Find your stock, keep supplies on hand, reserve donations and use warehouse materials for crafting, cooking, tool upgrades, Robin's buildings and optional Automate networks.

[b]Requires Stardew Valley 1.6.15+ and SMAPI 4.1.10+. Single-player and multiplayer personal/shared storage, with keyboard/mouse. English and Simplified Chinese are included; the UI follows the game language by default.[/b]

[b]New saves start with personal warehouses.[/b] The host can permanently enable sharing through Settings → Deposit or GMCM. Read and confirm the notice, then [b]save the game and reload that save[/b]. All personal stock, including offline players, merges into shared storage; unlocks and machine exclusions use the union, and minimum reserves use the highest value. Quality, custom item data and Protected Storage are retained. Bookmarks and carry targets remain personal. Existing EasyChests shared saves stay shared. This choice belongs to the save and cannot be undone through configuration; [b]back up your save before confirming[/b].

[size=4][b]Storage that grows with your farm[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]89 categories[/b] organized under ten navigation groups, with an All Categories overview. Miscellaneous/Mod Items, Ore, Basic Materials and Spring Crops start unlocked. Community Bundles and Museum Donations are also free in both new and existing saves. Unlock the remaining categories with gold; prices appear in the menu.
[*][b]72-slot pages[/b] with storage that expands as needed. There is no configured capacity limit; practical limits depend on memory, save size and game performance.
[*][b]All Items[/b] is selected every time the warehouse opens and is favorited as the first shortcut by default. It shows original stacks from ordinary, Protected, Community and Museum storage, excluding the backpack and Shipping Bin. Removing its favorite is saved per player; the opening view stays All Items. Ctrl-click withdraws by default (the controls can be swapped in Settings), Shift-click locates the source and quantity transfers use the original inventory. Backpack deposits follow normal classification.
[*][b]Category favorites and item bookmarks[/b] provide quick access. Star a category in the picker to add a tab to the main warehouse menu, ready to click after pressing G. Click a tab name to switch, use the arrows or scroll over the tabs for more favorites, and click its star to remove it. The next-page arrow follows the last visible tab, including partially filled pages. Favorites remain accessible when empty categories are hidden and also appear directly below the title in the picker's separate column, using its available height independently of the category groups. Item bookmarks reference the original stacks without duplicating stock.
[*][b]Global search[/b] by item name, qualified ID or category name. Withdraw, ship or locate actual stacks directly from results. Processing filters find ingredients for brewing, preserves, juice, pickles, drying and fish smoking without moving them.
[*][b]Quality stars and stack counts[/b] remain visible in storage, search, bookmark, filter and backpack views.
[*][b]Organization[/b] includes refill existing items, sort current category and sort warehouse. Ordinary gap compaction preserves item order without extra sorting or merging.
[/list]
Items whose category is still locked stay in Miscellaneous/Mod Items until unlocked and reclassified. Unknown items from other mods also have this fallback.

[size=4][b]Deposit and keep supplies on hand[/b][/size]
Press [b]V[/b] to deposit eligible backpack stock. Common tools, warehouse terminals and items marked [b]Carry All[/b] stay with you. Optional toolbar protection also retains the first 12 backpack slots.

Select an item and click [b]Carry[/b] to set a target quantity across all stacks and qualities of that item. Deposits move only the surplus; [b]Refill Carry[/b] retrieves available stock from ordinary warehouse categories. It respects purchased backpack capacity, stops when full or out of stock, and does not draw from collection reserves, Protected Storage or the shipping bin.

[b]Auto Deposit is off by default.[/b] Enable it on the main toolbar or in Settings to deposit when at most one purchased backpack slot is free. It follows carry and toolbar rules and never sells items.

[size=4][b]Craft, cook, upgrade tools and build from storage[/b][/size]
Ordinary warehouse materials are available to [b]vanilla crafting, cooking and Clint's tool upgrades[/b], enabled by default. [b]Robin's construction and building upgrades[/b] have a separate setting, also enabled by default. Material checks, displayed availability and consumption include eligible warehouse stock; backpack stock and vanilla material sources are used first.
The [b]beach bridge[/b] can use ordinary warehouse wood under the same construction setting. It still costs 300 wood, using the backpack first. Confirming rechecks available materials; declining consumes nothing. Protected Storage and donation reserves are excluded.

No physical terminal is needed for these uses. Tools still need to be carried for upgrades, and gold, placement, upgrade conditions and waiting times follow the game rules. Ordinary chests participate only where vanilla workbench/fridge rules already allow them. Other shops, gifts and donations are not handled automatically.

[size=4][b]Donation reserves and protected items[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Community Bundles[/b] keeps only the outstanding quantities at sufficient quality for unfinished bundle ingredients. Completed slots and choose-N bundles are accounted for; surplus returns to ordinary categories. Reserves are released when no longer needed, when joining Joja or when the setting is disabled.
[*][b]Museum Donations[/b] keeps one copy of each item the museum still accepts. Duplicates and donated items return to ordinary categories. Disable the setting to release its reserves.
[*]Both settings default to on. Reserved stock is excluded from crafting, cooking, tool upgrades, construction, carry restocking and Automate. Gold [b]C / M[/b] indicators show pending quantities; grey means none. Click an indicator to open its departure checklist, withdraw reserved items and submit them manually.
[*][b]Protected Storage[/b] is a separate free category for manual storage. Its contents are excluded from automatic material use and are not moved to ordinary categories by Sort Warehouse.
[/list]
[b]Use the departure checklist to withdraw reserved stock into your backpack in one action.[/b] After withdrawal, the result page offers a direct return to a refreshed checklist. Withdrawn items follow normal deposit, carry and toolbar rules, with no daily withdrawal lock or next-day return. When enabled, Auto Deposit can deposit these items again under the usual near-full-backpack conditions.

[b]Reserves and Protected Storage still allow manual withdrawal and explicit shipping.[/b] They do not donate items for you. Bookmarks only help you find items; carry targets govern deposit/restocking; machine permissions and reserves govern Automate. None of those item flags is a general protection against crafting, manual use or shipping. Check the selected-item status line and hold Shift over a tooltip for full protection details.

Use [b]Result details[/b] after depositing or refilling to inspect actual transferred quantities and reasons such as carry rules, toolbar protection, a full backpack, excluded stock or shortages. Click the C / M indicator to open a [b]departure checklist[/b] to review outstanding quantities/quality and withdraw reserved stock in one action. Items that do not fit remain stored; choose-N bundles do not require every alternative, and donations remain manual.

[size=4][b]Optional Automate integration[/b][/size]
Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/1063]Automate 2.6.1+[/url], buy a [b]Portable Warehouse Terminal for 2,500g[/b] in the warehouse menu and place it beside machines in an Automate network. Right-click a placed terminal to access the warehouse. The terminal has its own wood-and-copper sprite and green connection panel.

In personal mode, terminals use their placer's warehouse; multiple terminals placed by the same player share that inventory. Shared mode uses one inventory for all terminals. Machines draw from unlocked ordinary categories and deposit output back into the corresponding warehouse. Opening a warehouse pauses that warehouse's terminals; removing a terminal does not delete stock. Terminal networks do not merge with vanilla Junimo Chest networks.

Open [b]Settings → Materials → Vanilla Machine Settings[/b] to see the processing queue with a machine already selected. Choose a machine by its sprite and name on the left; switch to [b]Input permissions[/b] to check its supported inputs. Products are listed even before you own them, including fuel where applicable. Search by name or ID, or show only blocked inputs. [b]Allow all / Block all[/b] shows how many permissions will change and affects the current machine's full supported list, including other pages and inputs hidden by search or the blocked-only filter. Item-specific machine rules provide a link to the corresponding machine page. Changes save immediately and share the existing item-specific rules.

Select an item and open [b]Machines[/b] to allow or block its supported machines. Set [b]Machine Reserve[/b] to keep a minimum warehouse quantity away from Automate. For example, allow Keg and disable Preserves Jar for starfruit to permit automatic wine production while preventing jam production from warehouse stock.

The [b]Processing queue[/b] view uses arrows to connect input, machine and actual output for current batches. Waiting inputs show item sprites, available quantities and numbered priorities, linked from top to bottom by arrows. These numbers represent feeding priority. The view lists placed machines of the selected type, including unconnected machines, with current output quantities, locations, coordinates and remaining game time. Its complete waiting-input list uses available stock from this warehouse. [b]Drag rows to change the shared input priority for this machine type[/b]; hold near a list edge to scroll across pages. The [b]cross button[/b] also blocks the input across qualities using the same Machine Rules; re-enable it in [b]Input permissions[/b]. Priorities persist with the warehouse, quantities follow stock and current batches finish normally. Machine reserves and protected / Community / Museum stock are excluded; fuel and fairy dust are auxiliary inputs, not jobs. Native quantity, fuel and location checks still apply. Ordinary chests in the network remain outside these warehouse priorities and exclusions.

Supported machines are allowed by default. Permissions and reserves are shared across qualities of the same item, affect warehouse Automate inputs and do not restrict manual processing or crafting. Native recipe, fuel and quantity requirements still apply. Third-party custom Automate factories may need separate integration.

[size=4][b]Shipping[/b][/size]
Open the Shipping Bin view or use [b]Alt + left-click[/b] on a shippable stack; on Mac, use [b]Option + left-click[/b]. Items move into the farm's native shipping bin and sell overnight. You can retrieve them before then. Shipping works from the backpack, ordinary storage, protected storage and All Items/search/bookmark/filter results. Automatic deposit never ships items.

[size=4][b]Installation and updating[/b][/size]
[list]
[*]Install [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/2400]SMAPI 4.1.10+[/url] for Stardew Valley 1.6.15+.
[*]Close the game and back up your save.
[*]Create the game's Mods/EasyChests folder and extract the contents of [b]EasyChests-0.24.3.zip[/b] directly into it. Check that this folder contains manifest.json and EasyChests.dll.
[*]Launch through SMAPI, load a save and press G. A three-step introduction opens on first use. Replay it in Settings → Interface; the top [b]?[/b] button opens the full six-page guide.
[/list]
For updates, replace the mod files, keep your own [b]config.json[/b] and install only one copy. Existing warehouse IDs and purchase records are retained. No separate .NET runtime, Chests Anywhere, Bigger Backpack or StardewHack installation is required for EasyChests.

Automate is optional. Without it, storage, search, carry refill, crafting/building materials and shipping remain available; Machine Rules and Machine Reserve controls are hidden. Vanilla Machine Settings remains visible but disabled, with a hover explanation; it opens only after the Automate integration loads successfully. Physical terminals can still open the warehouse. Install the complete ZIP, including EasyChests.Automate.dll, which is the optional integration adapter. [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu 1.12.0+[/url] is also optional and adds configuration and keybinding editing. If you use Stardrop, enable the relevant mods in the active profile.

[size=4][b]Language, settings and controls[/b][/size]
The toolbar provides [b]Auto Deposit, Return to results and Settings[/b]. Settings groups Deposit, Browsing, Materials and Interface; buy terminals under Deposit and select language or replay the introduction under Interface. Changes save immediately, including slot size. Carry, bookmark and machine controls sit below the backpack. The selected stack shows its quality, source, quantity and separate deposit/crafting/machine/manual-shipping rules.

Help keeps a readable font size in small windows. Scroll over its text or use Up/Down to read long pages; Home/End jumps to the beginning/end and PageUp/PageDown changes guide pages. Hover a machine or product name to read it in full.

Within one warehouse menu, each category remembers its page; reduced page counts are clamped to the live inventory. A shipping round trip restores the original category, search, processing filter, page and return-to-results route. Machine settings remember the selected machine and retain queries, blocked-only filters and product positions separately for each machine. These browsing states are released when the whole warehouse menu closes.

Vanilla Machine Settings uses the available window height to show more machines, input permissions and waiting inputs; scrolling remains available in small windows and with UI scaling. Click or scroll the machine or product list to focus it. Up/Down moves one row, PageUp/PageDown moves a page, and Home/End jumps to that list's beginning/end. These keys stay with a focused text input. Esc releases input focus first, then returns to the previous panel; the carry amount dialog follows the same two-step return.

[b]Follow game is the default:[/b] a Chinese game UI selects Simplified Chinese; all other game languages select English. Auto mode responds to game language changes. The Settings → Interface Language button cycles [b]Follow game → English → Simplified Chinese[/b]. You can also select Language in GMCM or set it to "auto", "en" or "zh-CN" in config.json while the game is closed. Fixed choices override the game language. Old English configurations migrate once to Follow game on upgrade; old Chinese choices remain fixed. Select English again if you prefer it. Game and third-party item names, descriptions and machine names use their own translations.

[list]
[*][b]G:[/b] open the warehouse or return through menus. [b]V:[/b] deposit backpack items when free to interact.
[*][b]Item movement controls:[/b] Settings → Browsing and GMCM offer [b]Use Ctrl to move items[/b], enabled by default: Ctrl+left-click moves and left-click selects. Turn it off to move with left-click and select with Ctrl+left-click; the choice takes effect and saves immediately. Backpack deposits, warehouse withdrawals and Shipping Bin transfers use the same controls.
[*]Select an item, then use [b]Quantity[/b] to transfer a specified quantity, including shipping/taking back in Shipping Bin. The amount starts focused and selected: type to replace, Enter to transfer, Ctrl+A to select again and Tab to refocus. Quick transfers and Alt/Option shipments also update actual movement details.
[*][b]Shift + left-click:[/b] pick up a stack in ordinary storage; locate its original stack in All Items/search/bookmark/filter views. [b]Right-click:[/b] split stacks in ordinary storage.
[*][b]Alt/Option + left-click:[/b] ship a full stack. Alt+Ctrl prioritizes shipping; Alt+Shift keeps the Shift action.
[*][b]Left/Right or Tab/Shift+Tab:[/b] switch categories when no input or modal has focus. Locked categories are skipped by default.
[*][b]Mouse wheel, PageUp/PageDown or page buttons:[/b] change pages. Scroll over the backpack or use its arrow buttons to access additional purchased slots.
[*][b]Ctrl+F:[/b] focus search. [b]Enter:[/b] apply the active input. The search × clears text; the processing × clears only processing. Locate a result, then use Return to results to restore its query and page. Return to Category clears search and filters.
[*][b]Esc:[/b] return through dialogs, input focus, search and filters, then close. Letter keys such as G/V go to the focused text input.
[*][b]? / C / M:[/b] reopen help or open pending bundle/museum items.
[/list]
Edit keybindings in GMCM or the generated config.json using OpenKey, ArchiveKey, PreviousCategoryKey and NextCategoryKey. Custom bindings are preserved when migrating older default keys.

[size=4][b]Saves, compatibility and support[/b][/size]
You can add EasyChests to an existing save. Items use native save inventories, separated by player in personal mode; unlocks, carry rules, bookmarks and machine rules persist with normal game saves. UI preferences stay in the local config.json. Resetting configuration does not revert shared mode. Save before quitting.

[b]Before uninstalling, withdraw warehouse items, recover placed terminals and save.[/b] Removing the mod does not return stored items to your backpack. Reinstalling the same mod ID restores access to retained warehouse data.

EasyChests does not increase backpack or ordinary chest capacity. It supports purchased Bigger Backpack slots. [b]Controller navigation is unsupported.[/b] Custom Automate factories and crafting frameworks that bypass vanilla APIs need separate integration; unknown item classification is not a promise of universal mod compatibility.

[b]Multiplayer[/b]: The host and every online player need the same EasyChests version. Personal mode allows concurrent access to separate warehouses; each player manages their own unlocks, machine permissions, reserves and donation settings. Shared mode uses one queue and only the host changes shared rules. Cancel queued warehouse access with its waiting-window button, Esc or G. Menus pause Automate for the affected inventory, and shipping also needs farm shipping access. While waiting, crafting/building menus use vanilla material sources. Warehouse Automate runs only on the host. Split-screen follows the same modes with keyboard/mouse. Bookmarks and carry targets remain personal; UI preferences use the local configuration. Cursor items use synchronized temporary storage for recovery after interrupted access. Unsynchronized changes cannot be recovered after a client crash. Disconnect/reconnect, save/reload and high-latency play still need testing with a backup or test save.

If G does not open the warehouse, check SMAPI load errors, close other menus/text input and check keybinding conflicts. If Automate does not take an item, check the terminal network, storage category, machine permission, reserve quantity and recipe requirements.

For bug reports, include your operating system, Stardew Valley/SMAPI/EasyChests versions, optional integration versions, reproduction steps, expected/actual results and a [url=https://smapi.io/log]SMAPI log link[/url].

[b]自动入库默认关闭。[/b]在主界面顶部或「设置」中开启后，背包已购买格子剩余不超过一格时自动归档，遵守随身和工具栏保护规则，不会出售物品。

[size=4][b]可选 Automate 自动化[/b][/size]

个人模式按终端放置者使用其仓库，同一玩家的多个终端共用库存；共享模式下全部终端共用库存。机器读取对应仓库的已解锁普通分类，产出自动归档。打开仓库时暂停对应库存的终端自动化；拆除终端不删除仓库物品。终端网络不与原版祝尼魔箱网络合并。

打开[b]「设置 → 用料 → 原版机器设置」[/b]默认进入加工队列，并自动选中一台机器。左侧通过机器贴图和名称选择机器；切换到[b]「投料权限」[/b]可勾选它支持的投料产品，含适用的燃料；尚未持有的产品也可预先设置。支持按名称或 ID 搜索、只看禁止项；[b]「允许全部／禁止全部」[/b]显示将改变的权限数，作用于当前机器的完整产品列表，包含其他页面及被搜索或禁止项筛选隐藏的产品。物品侧的机器规则可直接跳转对应机器页面；修改立即保存，并与已有物品权限同步。

选中物品后打开[b]「机器操作」[/b]，逐项允许或禁止支持的机器；通过[b]「机器保留」[/b]设置不允许 Automate 消耗的最低仓库数量。例如杨桃只允许「小桶」、禁止「罐头瓶」，即可自动酿酒并避免自动做果酱。

[b]「加工队列」[/b]右侧用箭头连接原料、机器和当前实际产物；等待原料显示物品贴图、可用数量和优先级编号，用向下箭头连接，编号从上到下表示投料优先级。页面列出已放置的同类机器（含未连接的机器），显示当前产物数量、地点、坐标与剩余游戏时间，以及此仓库完整的等待原料和可用数量。[b]拖动原料行调整同类机器共用的投料优先顺序[/b]，拖到列表上下边缘可跨页滚动；[b]原料行右侧的叉号同时通过已有机器权限禁止该物品的所有品质[/b]，可在[b]「投料权限」[/b]中重新允许。顺序随仓库存档保存，数量随库存变化，当前加工继续完成。不消耗、社区、博物馆与机器保留量排除在队列之外；燃料、仙尘等辅助耗材不是加工任务。数量、燃料与地点仍由原版机器检查，同网络普通箱子的材料不受此仓库的排序和禁止规则控制。

默认允许全部支持的机器，同一物品的各品质共用权限与保留量。这些设置只限制本模组仓库的 Automate 进料，不限制手动加工或制作；仍需满足机器原有配方、燃料与数量条件。第三方自定义 Automate 工厂可能需要单独适配。

[b]卸载前先取出仓库物品、回收已放置终端并保存。[/b]移除模组不会将仓库物品自动退回背包，重新安装相同模组 ID 可再次访问存档中保留的数据。

不改变背包或普通箱子容量，支持 Bigger Backpack 已购买格数。[b]暂不支持手柄导航。[/b]第三方自定义 Automate 工厂、绕开原版 API 的制作框架需单独适配；能为未知物品提供兜底分类，不代表兼容所有模组行为。

[b]多人游戏[/b]：房主和全部在线玩家必须安装相同版本的 EasyChests。个人模式允许同时操作各自仓库，各自解锁分类、设置机器权限、最低保留及收集保留。共享模式使用同一访问队列，共享规则仅由房主修改。打开仓库的等待窗口可用按钮、Esc 或 G 取消排队。菜单暂停对应库存的 Automate，出货还需取得农场出货访问。制作／建造菜单等待期间使用原版材料；Automate 只在房主端运行。分屏遵循相同模式，使用键盘鼠标。收藏与随身目标按玩家保存，界面偏好按本机配置保存。游标物品通过原生存档库存暂存，可恢复已同步的中断操作；客户端崩溃前尚未传出的变更无法保证恢复。断线重连、保存重启及高延迟流程仍需使用备份或测试存档验证。

按 G 没有打开时，检查 SMAPI 加载错误、关闭其他菜单与文字输入，并检查快捷键冲突。Automate 不取料时，检查终端网络、物品分类、机器权限、保留量和配方条件。

反馈问题请提供操作系统、星露谷物语／SMAPI／EasyChests 版本、可选集成版本、复现步骤、预期与实际结果，以及 [url=https://smapi.io/log]SMAPI 日志链接[/url]。
